posts.author: Priyanshu Chourasia
posts.title: LLM from Scratch: Practical Engineering from Base Model to PPO RLHF (Phase 1)
posts.desc: Phase 1 of a hands-on series on building an LLM from scratch — from raw-text pretraining to PPO-based RLHF.
posts.intro: Base Model to PPO RLHF — Phase 1
posts.content:
Base Model. Before a language model can follow instructions, argue with you, or write code, it has to learn language itself — from raw text, with no notion of 'assistant' or 'user'. This is Phase 1 of a multi-part series where I build an LLM from scratch and walk through every stage: pretraining a base model, supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, and finally PPO-based RLHF.


The goal of this series isn't to reproduce a paper — it's practical engineering. Each phase covers the actual code, the failure modes I hit, and the compute/data tradeoffs that matter when you don't have a datacenter.


The Pipeline

Roughly, the journey looks like this:

  • Base model pretraining — next-token prediction on a large text corpus.
  • Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) — teaching the base model to follow instructions using curated prompt/response pairs.
  • Reward Modeling — training a model to score outputs by human preference.
  • PPO (RLHF) — using the reward model to fine-tune the policy with Proximal Policy Optimization.

In this first post, I set up the training stack and get a small base model learning from raw text — the foundation everything else builds on.

for step, batch in enumerate(dataloader):
    logits = model(batch.input_ids)
    loss = cross_entropy(logits, batch.labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    optimizer.zero_grad()
